fact: 1919年1月5日，柏林警察局长艾希霍恩被艾伯特政府免职，革命工长组织、独立社会民主党左翼与德国共产党随即发动大规模示威，演变为斯巴达克起义，约5万人参与；政府调国防军与自由军团镇压，至1月13日起义基本被扑灭。

sources.title: BBC Bitesize, The Weimar Republic 1918-1929: Challenges to the Weimar government
sources.quote: During 5 – 12 January 1919, 50,000 members of the post-World War One Communist Party, known as the Spartacists, rebelled in Berlin, led by Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht. The government was saved when, through the army, it armed bands of ex-soldiers, known as the Freikorps, who defeated the Spartacist rebels.

sources.title: Rosa Luxemburg, Wikipedia 条目（Spartacist uprising 节）
sources.quote: The dismissal of the popular but radical police chief of Berlin, Emil Eichhorn, by the Ebert government sparked a mass demonstration on 5 January ... By 13 January, the fighting was largely over and the revolt crushed.

fact: 1919年1月15日晚，李卜克内西与卢森堡在柏林威尔默斯多夫一处公寓被市民卫队发现并逮捕，随后被交给自由军团骑兵近卫狙击师；李卜克内西被枪杀，卢森堡被枪击后遗体被沉入兰德维尔运河，直至5月31日才被发现。

sources.title: Rosa Luxemburg, Wikipedia 条目（Spartacist uprising 节）
sources.quote: On the evening of 15 January, Luxemburg and Liebknecht were discovered in an apartment in the Wilmersdorf district of Berlin by the Wilmersdorfer Bürgerwehr ... There, she was shot in the head, and her body, weighted with stones, was thrown into the Landwehr Canal. Her body was not found until 31 May 1919.

sources.title: China.org.cn, Karl Liebknecht and Rosa Luxemburg: Marxist heroes remembered (2019-01-19)
sources.quote: Two days later, Liebknecht and Luxemburg were arrested, interrogated and tortured. Liebknecht was put in a car and killed by a shot from behind. Luxemburg was beaten with rifle butts before she was shot. Her corpse was dumped in a Berlin canal.

fact: 1919年1月德国举行国民议会选举；因柏林局势危险，国民议会于2月6日在魏玛开幕，2月11日艾伯特当选临时总统。

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, Weimar Republic
sources.quote: Germany was still dealing with outbreaks of violence in January 1919 when elections were held to select the members of a new national assembly. The capital of Berlin was still considered too dangerous, so members of the assembly agreed to hold their first meeting on February 6, 1919, in the central German town of Weimar.

sources.title: Weimar National Assembly, Wikiwand 条目
sources.quote: 6 February 1919 – Friedrich Ebert, as chairman of the Council of the People's Deputies, opened the first session of the National Assembly. ... 11 February 1919 – Friedrich Ebert was elected provisional Reich president.

fact: 1919年7月31日，国民议会以262票对75票通过宪法，8月11日在施瓦茨堡签署；宪法规定20岁以上男女公民均有选举权，并首次以第109条确立男女平权。

sources.title: Weimar National Assembly, Wikiwand 条目
sources.quote: On 31 July the Assembly passed the revised committee proposal for the constitution by a vote of 262 to 75, with USPD, DNVP and DVP against. ... 15 July Equality of the sexes Adopted what became Article 109

sources.title: Alpha History, Extracts from the Weimar Constitution (1919)
sources.quote: Article 109: All Germans are equal before the law. Men and women have the same fundamental civil rights and duties. ... Signed in Schwarzburg, August 11th 1919

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, Weimar Republic
sources.quote: The constitution allowed all citizens—both men and women—above the age of twenty to vote.

fact: 1919年6月28日德国在凡尔赛签约；总理谢德曼因拒绝接受条约辞职，由鲍尔接任并在协约国最后通牒下签署；德国各政治派别把条约称为“Diktat”（强加的和约）。

sources.title: The Peace Museum, Special Blog on Treaty of Versailles
sources.quote: The Government headed by Philip Scheidemann – Germany's first democratically elected head of government, was unable to agree on a common position, and Scheidemann himself resigned rather than agree to sign the treaty. ... They referred to the treaty as “the Diktat”, dictated peace, since its terms were presented to Germany on a take-it-or-leave-it basis.

sources.title: Historisches Lexikon Bayerns, Treaty of Versailles, 1919/20
sources.quote: The signing of the Peace Treaty of Versailles took place in the Hall of Mirrors on 28 June 1919.

fact: 魏玛宪法第48条允许总统在紧急状态下发布具有法律效力的紧急命令，即使暂时违反宪法中关于新闻自由、住宅不可侵犯等条款；国会可以简单多数撤销命令，但总统可先行解散国会。第48条在1919—1920年镇压革命与暴动时被实际使用。

sources.title: German History in Documents and Images, Weimar Germany (1918/19-1933), Introduction
sources.quote: Article 48 allowed the president to issue emergency decrees [Notverordnungen], even when they temporarily contravened specific parts of the constitution itself, such as freedom of the press and the right to privacy. The Reichstag still retained the power to rescind a presidential decree with a simple majority vote, but a president could circumvent that safeguard by preemptively dissolving parliament.

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, Weimar Republic
sources.quote: Presidential orders needed the approval of the chancellor or minister of the Reichstag, although the president could suspend parliamentary rule in case of an emergency. This provision was known as Article 48.

fact: 1919年11月18日柏林一封家书描述：写信人月薪225马克并另有时常发放的生活补贴，仍不足开支；黑市牛奶每升7马克，大米每磅约6马克（战前仅30芬尼）；每人每周配给一个面包，黄油凭证每人20克，牛奶只供给儿童和凭医生处方的病人。

sources.title: Montreal Holocaust Museum, Exploring the Evidence: letter of Wally Schorperle, Berlin, 18 November 1919
sources.quote: I receive a monthly salary of 225 marks and at times a bonus because of the high cost of living. ... A litre of milk costs 7 marks on the black market. Each person receives one loaf of bread a week. ... Rice costs about 6 marks a pound. During peacetime, before the war, it cost only 30 pfennig. ... we can purchase only 20 grams per person with our ration card.

fact: 1919年柏林面包实行法定最高价：上半年黑麦面包每公斤均价56.99芬尼、小麦面包60.67芬尼，较1918年同期分别上涨23.64%与20.42%；12月黑麦面包与小麦面包最高价进一步升至每公斤约81.85与106.35芬尼。

fact: 《凡尔赛条约》军事条款将德国陆军限制为10万人、海军1.5万人，废除义务兵役制，禁止拥有空军、坦克、装甲车、重炮与潜艇，并把莱茵兰设为非军事区；德国航空工业与军工产能因此被强制压缩。

sources.title: House of Lords Library, Treaty of Versailles: 100th Anniversary (2019)
sources.quote: Germany's armed forces: the German army was limited to 100,000 men and a navy of 15,000. Conscription was banned. Germany was not allowed an air force, tanks, armoured cars, heavy guns or submarines. ... The Rhineland became a demilitarised zone
